correctness.rationale: Torus automorphism gives three independent Haar phase differences; an independent arcsine angle and cosinusoidal factor yield exact joint density, then direct conditional integration proves CDF and the atom 5/36. For x in [C epsilon, eta], uniform Taylor expansion yields epsilon/(pi^2 x(1-x^2)) plus integrable error O(epsilon^2/x^2), proving the log coefficient; other portions are O(epsilon). An independent direct-complex-correlation checker makes 300000 residual checks plus CDF comparisons, but finite tests are only corroborative.

value.rationale: The entire joint law, the exact nonzero generalized-Barker success mass 5/36, all peak-sidelobe quantiles through one-dimensional quadrature, and the nonanalytic epsilon log(1/epsilon) near-optimal probability characterize the first four-chip continuous-phase model with genuinely coupled free sidelobes. These facts supply a calibrated random-search benchmark not furnished by an example of a Barker code or an L4 scalar variance.
